text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- Norway's trade surplus in June was almost ten percent lower than for the same month a year ago. Svein Longva, head of the government department Statistics Norway, says that despite increasing imports he sees no immediate danger for overspending.
- Mobile phone charges in Norway are among the lowest in Europe, where it is only cheaper in Cyprus and Portugal.

- Three Norwegian bishops have criticised Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland for not granting enough funding to elderly people. In this year's election campaign Jagland has suggested increasing monthly state pensions by 700 crowns.

- Norway's largest commercial bank, Den norske Bank, and insurer Storebrand have not been successful in the private investor market. During the first six months of the year, the two finance giants only managed to win four percent of the 10 billion crowns invested in different funds.

- Private investor Kjell Inge Roekke and holding company Aker RGI want to take control of three fishing vessels owned by competitor Emerald Resource Management (ERM). Representaives from both companies are now in Seattle in the United States, most likely to negotiate a deal.
